name: MANGAL: the Tuesday gold season
one_line: One word, MANGAL, which means auspicious and in eight Indian languages also names Tuesday, lettered in nine scripts, runs Naira's festive season from Karwa Chauth to the first muhurats; every tile is a drawn object from Mummy's house with a real, photographed Naira piece inside it, and the spine is the owner's own line: Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.
big_idea: In Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu, Punjabi and Urdu, Tuesday is named for Mangal, and mangal also means auspicious. The festive season is the stretch of the year when every Indian house waits for an auspicious day and takes the good gold out of the locker for it. Naira's answer is the owner's top-scored line, Not locker gold. Tuesday gold.: jewellery for the ordinary days in between, which in eight languages are already called mangal. So the season gets one title, MANGAL, written the way PTAT wrote MILNI: one word in every script of the families who read it. The key art (P1) sets it in nine scripts; after that every tile carries a compact MANGAL lockup with ONE script under it, a different language each post (Punjabi for Karwa Chauth, Marathi for the almirah, Tamil for the thali, Gujarati for the faral dabba...), so the finished grid spells the word in ten languages and nine scripts, and every caption ends 'Today's mangal: <language>' as a collect-them-all hook. Under the title runs a numbered sub-series, HOUSE RULES N° 01-10: the rules every Indian mother enforced (the good gold lives in the locker; the dabba never goes back empty; shagun always ends in one; one ring means I've reached, two rings means call me back; the good box is never thrown away), each staged on the object itself, drawn, with the real piece as the punchline. The world has one honesty rule that is also its look: everything drawn is from Mummy's house, everything photographed is for sale. Every Tuesday post lands in the right-hand column, so column 3 of the finished grid is the four Mangalvaars of the season.
why_it_fits: BRAND: it turns up what Naira already owns instead of borrowing PTAT's look. Velista caps + Cormorant italic turn + Jost stay the type system; the lockup's brackets are the bag's own coral tulips and a drawn almirah key with a latkan (the couture house's tassel); grounds are Naira's own families pushed festive (Red Room oxblood #4B191A, Lilac 'on' plum #2E2338, exhibition bottle green #2E4238, ad marigold #E8973A, bag coral #E4886F, catalogue lilac #C9B6CB and blush #F2CFC4). No black ground, no sand, no stickers, no stamps: one object, one real piece, one lockup per tile. Claims stay inside the listing words ('18k gold tone plated', 'rhodium plated', 'ruby-red cubic zirconia', 'mint, not emerald'), no price-led art, offers only in captions. DATA: the best ad in the account is an everyday Indian object + one piece + one witty Indian line ('Anaar, pre-peeled.', Rs 335 per purchase, ROAS 4.52) and concept statics beat plain 1.44x to 0.57x; this grid is that formula as a system. Ruby is the hero stone (Ruby 8 of 13 tennis bracelets since 16 Oct, 3 of 3 huggies) and leads P1, P6, P12; the four bestsellers with deep stock (Woven Gold Hoops 63, Prism Riviere 67, Heartbead 25, Brushed Gold Huggies 35) each get a tile; the biggest unsold stock lines (Baguette Tennis Necklace 70 in stock, 0 sold; Kiss Knot Bangle 40/0; Silk Mesh Cuff 40/0; Bold Nocturne Chain 53/2) get guide slots. Women 35-54 made 64% of purchases and Maharashtra is 46% of orders: the objects are their childhood homes (Godrej-era almirah, Diwali faral dabba, the missed-call code of 2006, the Marathi mangalashtak's 'Shubh mangal saavdhan'), Marathi script leads, and Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad buyers each find their own script. Posting Tue/Fri/Sun at 12:00 or 19:00 IST matches when buyers order (Sunday is 27% of orders; peaks 12:00, 18:00, 21:00). Gift-driving posts land early enough for 3-5 day delivery; later festive posts say honestly when a piece will arrive. OWNER TASTE: Indian everyday-object wit with restraint (dabba, missed call, steel almirah, Tuesday gold are all from the owner's own 16 Oct caption doc, scored 9-10), lilac and plum, moody night grounds, deck tulips, chic still life (the two plates she loved are reused: 'RSVP' invitation plate for P11, rangoli Prism for P5), exact facts. Avoided: soan papdi, spice props, black grounds, full faces (worn shots cropped chin-down or from behind), anything that reads AI-made (jewellery is always the real listing photo; only objects are drawn). REFERENCE: PTAT's system, translated not copied: a season title in many scripts (MILNI -> MANGAL), one lockup with two bracketing motifs on most tiles (marigolds + mehndi hand -> coral tulips + almirah key), the event told in waves with a different job per tile (key art, guide 'vol 1', nostalgia hook, proof reel, finale), photos framed by line drawings (PTAT's armoire -> Naira's almirah mirror), a steel serving surface as a jewellery guide (PTAT's tray -> a five-katori thali), and a checkerboard of weight in every row.

grid_system.type_system: Brand faces only for Latin text, three roles: VELISTA 400 (kit/fonts/Velista.woff2), caps only, no ₹, no middle dot, no em dash: headlines 92-120 px on 1080 (anything meant to read in the grid >= 90 px), lockup word 92 px (compact) to 210 px (key art), letter-spacing .02-.04em, line-height .95. CORMORANT GARAMOND ITALIC 400, lowercase: the turn / the setup line, 40-56 px, always ending in a full stop. JOST: eyebrow 500 24 px tracking .32em uppercase (one per slide max, uses 'N°' with the degree sign because Jost has no №), product label 400 22 px tracking .14em uppercase, fact lists 300/400 24-28 px; prices in Jost with ₹ falling back to Poppins via var(--nf-font-label). HANDWRITING (inside drawings only, never as a headline): Kalam 400, 22-30 px, in red-pen #B8604A or plum, for Mummy's labels on the locker list, the calendar circles and the saved boxes. SCRIPT VOICE (the MANGAL lettering only; owner sign-off needed because it adds faces): the Tiro superfamily, drawn by one foundry to harmonise across scripts: Tiro Devanagari Marathi (in kit) and Tiro Devanagari Hindi, Tiro Gurmukhi, Tiro Bangla, Tiro Kannada, Tiro Telugu, Tiro Tamil (Google Fonts); Gujarati in Noto Serif Gujarati 600; Urdu in Gulzar (Nastaliq); Malayalam in Noto Serif Malayalam 600. Every script word is set with a cream #FBF3EC keyline (-webkit-text-stroke with paint-order: stroke fill) and a misregistered second-ink copy offset 6-9 px down-right, the same treatment as the Latin MANGAL, so ten languages read as one lockup. Every Indic word must be rendered in Chromium (HarfBuzz) and checked glyph by glyph by a native reader before posting. EXACT STRINGS: Marathi मंगळ (Tuesday मंगळवार), Hindi मंगल (मंगलवार), Gujarati મંગળ (મંગળવાર), Bengali মঙ্গল (মঙ্গলবার), Kannada ಮಂಗಳ (ಮಂಗಳವಾರ), Telugu మంగళ (మంగళవారం), Punjabi ਮੰਗਲ (ਮੰਗਲਵਾਰ), Urdu منگل (Tuesday is also منگل), Tamil மங்களம் (auspiciousness; Tuesday is செவ்வாய்), Malayalam മംഗളം (Tuesday is ചൊവ്വാഴ്ച), Marathi finale शुभमंगल सावधान, envelope print शुभ, calendar month नोव्हेंबर.

posts.concept: The season's title, lettered the way PTAT lettered MILNI: one word in the scripts of every family it is for. MANGAL means auspicious, and in eight of these languages it is also the name for Tuesday, which is why the season opens on a Tuesday and why Naira's thesis is Tuesday gold. Slide 2 is the dictionary page that explains the double meaning (and is honest that Tamil and Malayalam name Tuesday differently); slide 3 is the first piece of the season, with the line 'No muhurat needed.'

posts.caption:
Diwali is five days long, so we laid it out the only way an Indian house would. One thali, five katoris.

Dhanteras, Choti Diwali, Lakshmi Puja, Padwa, Bhai Dooj. One piece for each day. Swipe through the katoris, the menu is on the last one.

And because no Indian mother has ever let anyone leave after one serving: take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off, with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout.

Today's mangal: Tamil, மங்களம். In Chennai a thali is something else entirely. This one is lunch.

[ five pieces · 18k gold tone plated, one in two tones · ek aur ]
posts.alt_text: Slide 1: a top-down drawing of a steel thali on a dark red block-printed ground. Five steel katoris, numbered one to five on the rim, each hold a real piece: a gold-tone knot bangle, a fine crystal tennis bracelet, a ruby-red baguette necklace, a two-tone link necklace and a fine bracelet with a two-heart bow. Text: House rule 03, the Mangal Thali, vol 1. Five days. Five katoris. And still, someone will ask: ek aur? Slides 2 to 6: one katori per day of Diwali, each with its piece and price. Slide 7: a cream menu card titled Today's Thali listing the five pieces with prices.
posts.why: Tue 3 Nov leaves 3-5 working days for delivery before Diwali (8 Nov) without printing any order-by date. It is the season's guide post, PTAT's 'Accessory Guide vol 1' translated into the most Indian serving device there is, with a numbered legend (PTAT's [01]-[04] device, legitimate because it keys the days). It carries the offer because BUY3 baskets are already happening (BUY3 used in 9 of 124 orders, BUY2 13) and 69% of orders are a single piece; the 'ek aur' rule makes the offer a joke instead of a shout. Four of the five pieces have deep stock and almost no sales (Kiss Knot 40/0, Fine Tennis 20/0, Baguette Tennis Necklace 70/0, Duo Link 18/2); Ribbon Bead at ₹799 gives brothers an entry price (men 18-24 converted at ROAS 2.21). Tamil script on the thali because in Tamil Nadu 'thali' is the wedding necklace, a joke for the caption.
